Certainly! Here is the information about **photosynthesis**, represented as (subject, predicate, object) triples:

1. (Photosynthesis, is, a biological process)
2. (Photosynthesis, occurs in, plants)
3. (Photosynthesis, occurs in, algae)
4. (Photosynthesis, occurs in, some bacteria)
5. (Photosynthesis, converts, light energy)
6. (Photosynthesis, converts, carbon dioxide)
7. (Photosynthesis, converts, water)
8. (Photosynthesis, produces, glucose)
9. (Photosynthesis, produces, oxygen)
10. (Photosynthesis, takes place in, chloroplasts)
11. (Chloroplasts, contain, chlorophyll)
12. (Chlorophyll, absorbs, light energy)
13. (Light energy, drives, chemical reactions)
14. (Carbon dioxide, enters, leaves through stomata)
15. (Water, is absorbed by, roots)
16. (Glucose, is used in, cellular respiration)
17. (Oxygen, is released through, stomata)
18. (Photosynthesis, has, two stages)
19. (First stage, is called, light-dependent reactions)
20. (Second stage, is called, Calvin cycle)
21. (Light-dependent reactions, take place in, thylakoid membranes)
22. (Calvin cycle, takes place in, stroma)
23. (Light-dependent reactions, require, sunlight)
24. (Calvin cycle, uses, ATP)
25. (Calvin cycle, uses, NADPH)
26. (ATP, is produced in, light-dependent reactions)
27. (NADPH, is produced in, light-dependent reactions)
28. (ATP, provides, energy for the Calvin cycle)
29. (NADPH, provides, reducing power for the Calvin cycle)
30. (Calvin cycle, fixes, carbon dioxide)
31. (Calvin cycle, produces, glucose)
32. (Photosynthesis, reduces, carbon dioxide to carbohydrate)
33. (Photosynthesis, is vital for, life on Earth)
34. (Photosynthesis, forms, basis of most food chains)
35. (Photosynthesis, maintains, atmospheric oxygen levels)
36. (Photosynthesis, influences, carbon cycle)
37. (Photosynthesis, can be affected by, light intensity)
38. (Photosynthesis, can be affected by, carbon dioxide concentration)
39. (Photosynthesis, can be affected by, temperature)
40. (Photosynthesis, can be limited by, water availability)
41. (Photosynthesis, evolved, billions of years ago)
42. (Cyanobacteria, were among, first organisms to perform photosynthesis)
43. (Oxygenic photosynthesis, produces, oxygen)
44. (Anoxygenic photosynthesis, does not produce, oxygen)
45. (Anoxygenic photosynthesis, occurs in, some bacteria)
46. (Photosynthesis, supports, aerobic respiration)
47. (Photosynthesis, is described by, the equation 6CO₂ + 6H₂O + light → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂)
